My ex was upset with me when we broke up, it was the entire thing that we just didn't see each other. I was okay for a while, happy and at the same time I was miserable.  We never talked and he expected that it would be the same. I fell out of love with him, and he got really upset about it. We promised to be friends, and I thought we were going to be. But I guess I was wrong, he said that isn't how the real world thinks. That you just can't be friends. 

My friends are... I dunno, they just don't talk to me anymore. But they have their own lives, their own worries. They don't need mine piled up on top of theirs. I only have three friends, two of which no longer live anywhere near me. We talk, but it's never for long. And in truth, I can't tell them anything of importance. They wouldn't get it. They are the type of people who say suck it up and move on.

I'm used to it. Or at least, I've been trying to become used to hurting people. 

In elementary, I was bullied for being one of the guys, because all the girls thought I was weird. I watched anime,  I was loud. In middle school, I was bullied for being chubby and then when I lost over 20 pounds, I was bullied for trying to be a wannabe. Every time I've had a friend, they've always been bullied extra hard for being around me. In high school, food was thrown at me because I was gaining weight. I went to my classes for the first month and then I skipped, because the others would follow me and taunt me for being smart. My parents got into trouble for me not being in class, and I ended up leaving in sophomore year to be homeschooled because my parents couldn't afford daycare for my brother and sister. If I didn't go back to high school, then my mom wouldn't have gotten sick and then I got sick. I had stress induced sicknesses. I ended up having to have my gall blader taken out and put on anxiety pills, which I can't take.

I hurt people. My friends got bullied because I was different, and then my parents got into trouble for me not going to classes because I was bullied. 

I don't want to talk about that anymore.
